claims.text: The starting material is a single-phase, equiatomic CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy.
As-processed CoCrFeNi lacks inherent self-lubricating phases.
Dispersing nanoscale WS2 in CoCrFeNi will produce a protective, low-shear tribofilm during sliding.
Uniformly distributed WS2 particles will facilitate in-situ formation of a lubricious interfacial tribolayer.
The WS2-derived tribolayer will persist from room temperature through 800 °C.
Mechanical and thermal activation during sliding will cause dispersed WS2 to form a thin lubricious film.
Easy-shear basal planes in the WS2-derived film will reduce interfacial shear.
The lubricious film may adapt its crystal structure at elevated temperatures.
Temperature-induced microstructural evolution in unmodified CoCrFeNi causes its friction to increase.
Temperature-induced microstructural evolution in unmodified CoCrFeNi causes its wear to increase.
WS2-modified CoCrFeNi will have a lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
WS2-modified CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The friction and wear advantage of the WS2-modified alloy will be greater near 800 °C than at room temperature.
The intervention will remain beneficial only if WS2 is chemically stable and does not oxidize into a non-lubricious phase.
Extreme oxidation or excessive applied load can disrupt the lubricious film and eliminate its benefit.
